sentences.text: Shri Virendra Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.
Ms. Bhagyashree Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.

Heard on I.A. No.2767/2024,
which is third application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C for grant of suspension of sentence filed on behalf of appellant Rajesh.
The first two applications were dismissed as withdrawn.

2. The appellant has been convicted under Sections 304B, 306, 498A of IPC & Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years, 7 years, 3 years and fine of Rs.1000/- in each sections with default stipulation.
3. According to the prosecution story, the deceased was married with accused on 11.05.2013.
She burnt on 04.01.2016 and she was brought to the Civil Hospital, Khachroad.
Initially she was taken to Primary Health Center from where she was referred to District Hospital Ujjain where she was declared dead.
4. Counsel for the appellant submits that as per the testimony of the witnesses the financial condition of the appellant is much better than the complainant side.
They themselves had stated that at the time of marriage there was no demand of dowry and there was no physical torture to the deceased.

The appellant has already remained in jail for period of three years and the appeal is of year 2022, final hearing of the appeal is likely to take time and, therefore, the jail sentence of the appellant be suspended.

In support of his submission, he has placed reliance on M. Radha Hari Seshu vs. State of Telangana (2020) 8 SCC 114 where the jail sentence of the appellant was suspended after completion of jail sentence of more than 3 & 1/2 years and he was enlarged on conditional bail.

entities.text: M. Radha Hari Seshu vs. State of Telangana (2020) 8 SCC 114
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Counsel for the State opposes the prayer and submits apart from the mother of the deceased Anita Bai (PW-1), Kiran (PW-2), the independent witnesses PW-3 (Vikramsingh), PW-4 Sanjay have also supported the prosecution case.
It is alleged that the appellant and family members used to torture the deceased because of not bringing dowry and also for not giving birth to a child.

6. Per contra counsel for the appellant submits that there are contradictions in the statement of Vikram Singh (PW-3) and Sanjay (PW-4).
7.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration that Anita Bai (PW-1),
Kiran (PW-2) have made specific allegation that deceased used to be harassed and tortured for not Rajesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187422267/
1 bringing dowry soon before the death, apart from that Vikram Singh (PW-3) & Sanjay (PW-4) have also deposed that deceased also used to be physically torture and was subjected to cruelty for not bringing dowry and not giving birth to a child, this Court does not find a case for grant of suspension of jail sentence.

entities.text: Rajesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The facts of the case of M. Radha Hari Seshu (supra) are different.

In the said case,
there was no allegation that the deceased was being subjected to cruelty for not giving birth to a child.
In the present case, prima facie the prosecution witnesses have proved its case.
No case is made out for grant of suspension of jail sentence.
Accordingly, the IA is dismissed.
